sentences.text: So why are airplane windows round, and not square?
In nineteen fifty-four, two Comets, the world's first jet airliners, broke apart in midair.
Every flight, the cabin gets pumped full of air, then let down again.
That flexes the metal, over and over.
At sharp corners, the stress bunches up, and tiny cracks start to grow.
Round corners spread the stress out evenly.
So pretty much every airliner since has rounded windows.
